scope: Design an evaluation and release decision for an SKU matching service. All counts below are constructed examples, not live model measurements.

business_policy.in_scope: All valid requests for the supported product family, including requests with insufficient matching evidence, remain in scope.
business_policy.valid_outcomes: auto_match with a real target ID, or hold with a reason. A valid request lacking a required distinguishing attribute must be held. An empty response is never a valid hold.
business_policy.hold_correctness: For this synthetic task, full policy correctness requires auto_match when complete evidence satisfies the matching rule for exactly one target. A hold is policy-correct when required evidence is insufficient or no unique match can be established. A syntactically valid hold can therefore still be an avoidable, policy-incorrect hold; its operational cost is counted either way.
business_policy.matching_rule: An automatic match requires an exact canonical product code, color and pack_count match to exactly one existing target. An absent color is valid input but insufficient evidence for automatic matching.
business_policy.invalid_input: Non-JSON input and duplicate request IDs are outside this batch's agreed input contract. They are counted and reported as predeclared exclusions, not silently dropped after seeing model results.
business_policy.release_requirement: For the frozen deployment rule, the error probability among automatic matches must be at most 0.01 with a one-sided 95% confidence bound. Coverage and expected loss must be reported separately. A higher mean score cannot waive a known identity-contract violation.

scenario_a_accounting.description: A complete synthetic replay with adjudicated outcome counts. This is separate from the pilot in scenario B.
scenario_a_accounting.hold_policy_correctness: Not provided; the aggregate hold count alone does not distinguish justified holds from avoidable holds.

scenario_b_release_pilot.description: A different, independently sampled pilot; do not pool it with scenario A.
scenario_b_release_pilot.sampling_assumptions: For this planning exercise, these are IID representative automatic matches under a rule frozen before sampling, with trusted error labels. Production validation must check those assumptions.
scenario_b_release_pilot.team_claim: Zero observed errors establishes compliance with the release requirement.

stress_set.description: Cases were deliberately collected to exercise difficult interactions. Deployment stratum weights are not available.
stress_set.team_claim: The unweighted mean of this set is the service's production accuracy.

draft_evaluation_plan.reference: Run two prompts on the same model family and accept agreement as an independently correct label; inspect only disagreements.
draft_evaluation_plan.scorer: Assign zero to every hold or empty response, and remove information-insufficient requests from the quality denominator.
draft_evaluation_plan.selection: Change the confidence threshold after every candidate, evaluate on the same holdout, and keep whichever threshold has the best holdout result.
draft_evaluation_plan.available_partition_groups: Source product families can be used to keep related requests together when splitting data.
